title: The Pinecrest Footbridge
story:
Morning light broke over the lower mountain slopes in soft shades of grey and pale amber. James sat up on his rocky ledge, feeling the damp morning air against his fur, and carefully opened Barnaby's brass compass. He watched the slender needle tremble before settling steadily toward the south, pointing the way higher into the towering pine forest above.

He climbed past mossy roots that gripped the mountain earth. He climbed past wild blueberry bushes wet with early rain. He climbed past ancient boulders worn smooth by centuries of highland runoff. With every step upward, the distant smells of Oakhaven's chimney smoke faded, replaced by the sharp, resinous perfume of pine needles and damp stone.

By midday, a deep, roaring sound filled the forest. The dirt trail narrowed to a mossy embankment leading to Pinecrest Stream, a rushing torrent of white water cascading over slick grey rocks. A creaking, weathered timber footbridge spanned the narrow gorge. Pausing at the edge, James brought out his green sea-glass, peering through its smooth lens to watch the emerald spray glint in the filtered sunlight before carefully stepping onto the wooden planks.

Crossing with deliberate care as the bridge vibrated gently under his paws, James reached a dry stone trailhead shelter built directly against the cliff face. He sat beneath its overhanging roof as cool mist began to drift through the pine canopy, pulled out his charcoal, and marked the stream on his map. He did not look back down toward the valley below; his eyes remained fixed on the winding trail ahead.
location: A stone trailhead shelter beside Pinecrest Stream on Cloudveil Ridge
